kind: synthetic: every number below comes from the assumptions in scenarios.json; nothing is measured in the Demerzel repository, and no weekly output of the project was read
rounding: probabilities to 6 decimals, weeks and costs to 2, courses and ratios to 4, distances in standard errors to 2; exact fractions are rounded half to even
arithmetic: exact figures are counts of equally likely coin histories (whole numbers and fractions); the simulation draws from random.Random(seed).random(); floats come from + - * /, math.sqrt and math.fsum

plan.note: Scale of the example only. The project question's plan, 25 courses in each of 21 departments, is a figure from a draft curriculum specification that is not in the repository. The pinned repository does not state it: it holds 23 department records, 21 of them with a course folder, and its README counts 23 departments and 21 course tracks with no number of courses per track. The 25, the 21 and the weekly output are inputs of this lesson, not counts made in the repository, and no weekly output of the project was measured.

simulation.note: Seeds were fixed before the first run. Every draw is random.Random(seed).random(); a week with d drafts uses the top d bits of one draw as d fair coins.

single_look.definition: Probability that a rule fires at ONE week-end chosen in advance, on plan. Counted exactly; the simulated share is the same event in the first week of each simulated plan.

weekly_limit.formula: P(at least one alarm in T weeks) = 1 - (1 - a)^T, a = alarm chance of one on-plan week; average run length = 1 / a; mean delay = 1 / (alarm chance of one slow week)

prediction_band_every_week.definition: Alarm at the first week-end at which the cumulative shortfall is more than z standard deviations of the on-plan cumulative output. The looks share their history, so 1 - (1 - a)^T does not apply; the sum of the single looks is only an upper bound.

tolerance.definition: Alarm at the end of the first week at which the cumulative shortfall is at least the tolerance, a fixed number of courses.

cumulative_sum.definition: Page's scheme on the weekly scores (shortfall minus reference value): alarm when the sum of the scores is at least the decision interval above its lowest earlier value. The reference value 1 is half the weekly loss of the slowdown to detect, (5 - 3) / 2.
cumulative_sum.recursion: C(0) = 0; C(t) = max(0, C(t-1) + planned - output(t) - reference_value); alarm when C(t) >= decision interval

change_week.definition: Exact, for the two calibrated rules. Delay = slow weeks seen when the alarm comes, among runs silent when the slowdown starts.

milder_slowdown.note: Exact, for the two calibrated rules, slowdown from the same week as in the main tables.

bursty_output.note: The strongest objection made concrete. Same mean of 5 courses a week, but delivered in batches: in one week out of four (chance 1/4, independently) a batch of 40 drafts is in work, each finished with probability 1/2; in the other weeks nothing is finished.

costs.note: Assumed, for the worked example on choosing a threshold. Expected cost of a rule = (1 - probability_of_a_slowdown) * P(false alarm during the plan) * false_alarm_cost + probability_of_a_slowdown * mean delay * slow_week_cost. A deliberately crude model: one slowdown at first_slow_week or none, one review per false alarm.
costs.formula: expected cost = (1 - q) * P(false alarm during the plan) * false-alarm cost + q * mean delay * cost of a slow week

hypothesis_test.note: Written into the research cycle's hypothesis at 2026-10-14T02:37:54Z, before any file of this fixture existed.

hand_computed_case.note: Worked by hand in the README: 2 drafts in work, 1 course a week planned, 3 weeks, 64 equally likely histories.

reflection_principle.note: A walk that moves one step up or down with equal chances. The reflection principle gives P(highest value in n steps >= c) = P(end >= c) + P(end > c), a closed form the recursion must reproduce exactly.

simulation_against_exact.note: The simulation uses three seeded sets of runs, so these comparisons are not independent of one another. About 1 comparison in 20 is expected outside its 95% range by chance.

transfer_task.note: Hypothetical two-person team for the learner task. Not Streeling data and not a forecast.
